neighbours.label: the moment of direct formal address to an audience in a speech (Mr. Speaker, / Ladies and gentlemen, / Thank you, and God bless)
fire: Madam President, honourable members, I thank you for the opportunity to address this house.
Distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, welcome to the opening of our new hospital.
Thank you all, and may God continue to bless this great nation of ours.
Mr. Chairman, I yield the remainder of my time to the gentleman from Ohio.
My dear friends and fellow citizens, tonight we begin a new chapter together.
Your Honour, with respect, my learned colleague has misread the statute entirely.
Members of the committee, I appreciate your patience during this long hearing.
Excellencies, delegates, ladies and gentlemen, it is a privilege to open this summit.
quiet: The president of the assembly thanked members for the chance to speak in the house.
Guests and staff gathered on Tuesday for the opening of the new hospital.
The crowd clapped politely as the candidate left the stage after the rally.
The chairman gave the remaining time to the congressman from Ohio.
The mayor told reporters that the city would begin a new chapter this year.
The judge noted that the lawyer for the defence had misread the statute.
The committee members waited patiently through the long hearing on Monday.
Delegates from forty countries arrived in the capital for the summit.

notes: Top examples: 'Thank you,' closing a speech, 'Meine sehr geehrten Damen und', 'my learned friend', 'Ladies and Gentlemen,', '(Applause.)'. Probe: 'Mr. Speaker,' 1.21, 'Ladies and gentlemen' 0.64, but a third-person report of a speech reached 0.25, so near misses may leak.
